table.ruleB: 6 chambers, holding limit 10,8,12,6,9,7; pupation 7,6,9,5,7,5; return 3,2,4,2,3,2; start 3,6,6,2,2,1; moult limit 38; all LARVAL; waste 0; quarter/half rounded down

table.ruleA: Add the cycle's charge row to each crucible; working volume not enforced
table.ruleB: Add the cycle's feed row to each chamber; holding limit not enforced

table.ruleA: Sequential 1..6; if melt > volume (strict), excess goes to next crucible before it is handled, melt set to volume; crucible 6 excess to slag
table.ruleB: Sequential 1..6; if mass > limit (strict), excess added to next chamber before it is handled, mass set to limit; chamber 6 excess to waste

table.ruleA: Read melt after Step 2; BASE and melt >= upper -> SUPERHEATED; SUPERHEATED and melt <= lower -> BASE; else unchanged; log (cycle, crucible, before, after)
table.ruleB: Read mass after step 2; LARVAL and mass >= pupation -> PUPAL; PUPAL and mass <= return -> LARVAL; else unchanged; log (cycle, chamber, before, after)

table.ruleA: Compute all six amounts first from start-of-step melt (BASE quarter, SUPERHEATED half, rounded down on the melt), then apply simultaneously: BASE amount to slag, SUPERHEATED amount to previous crucible (crucible 1's to slag)
table.ruleB: Sequential 1..6, each amount computed from mass at that moment and applied immediately: LARVAL quarter to waste, PUPAL half to previous chamber (chamber 1's to waste)
table.difference: Wording differs (simultaneous vs sequential) but functionally equivalent: transfers only go from n to n-1, and n-1 has already been processed when n is reached, so no chamber's amount is ever computed after it has received anything. Every chamber's 'mass at that moment' equals its start-of-step mass.

table.ruleA: Sum all six; if > 38 (strict), every crucible halved rounded down, removed melt to slag, log cycle; applies to all six
table.ruleB: Sum all six; if > 38 (strict), every chamber halved rounded down, removed mass to waste, log cycle; applies to all six

table.ruleA: (a) end melts 1-6, (b) end states, (c) state changes, (d) tap cycles, (e) slag total, (f) balance check
table.ruleB: (a) end masses 1-6, (b) end stages, (c) stage changes, (d) moult cycles, (e) waste tally, (f) balance check

result.probeWhy: Heavy loads push every position SUPERHEATED/PUPAL in cycle 1, so in Step 4 every position both sends half to its predecessor and receives from its successor, the exact case where A's simultaneous and B's sequential wording could diverge; it also drives cascading overflow in Step 2, repeated halvings, a zero-input cycle to trigger reverse state changes. A 200,000-case random test (starts and inputs 0-9) also found zero differences.
result.differingRule: None. The only wording difference is Step 4: A computes everything first and applies it all at once, while B handles each position in turn. These are equivalent because returned melt only moves from position n back to n-1, and n-1 has always been handled before n.
result.trust: Both routes agree. The table argument proves the Step 4 wording difference has no effect for any input. It also ran 200,000 random starting and input tables (values 0-9) and found zero differences.
